recipes.name: Easy Oreo Truffles
ingredients_raw: 16 ounces cream-filled chocolate sandwich cookies (such as Oreo®), divided

steps.text: Melt chocolate in a saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally, 4 to 6 minutes.
While the chocolate is melting, place 9 cream-filled sandwich cookies in a food processor and blend until finely crushed. Transfer crumbs to a bowl and reserve for decorating.

Add remaining cookies to the food processor and blend until finely crushed. Transfer crumbs to a large bowl and stir in cream cheese; mix until well-blended. Roll mixture into 42 balls, about 1-inch in diameter.
Place each ball in melted chocolate and use two forks to roll it until fully coated. Lift the ball with both forks and allow excess chocolate to drip off.
Place coated truffle on a wax paper-lined baking sheet and sprinkle with reserved cookie crumbs to decorate. Repeat to make remaining truffles.
Refrigerate truffles until firm, at least 1 hour. Keep in the refrigerator until just before serving. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Oreo Truffles
raw_recipe.description: These delicious Oreo truffles are bite-sized chocolaty treats easily made with 3 simple ingredients: Oreo cookies, cream cheese, and melted chocolate.

video.description: These truffles are very easy and delicious. You can't go wrong with OREO, cream cheese and chocolate!

review.reviewBody:
crowd pleaser. everyone always begs for these but i recommend the following:

1. don't use double stuf oreos (they fall apart, it's messy, just don't try it)

2. you can subsitute almond bark for the outer coating, it's delicious.

3. the chocolate outer coating is really really hard to put on the oreo balls so first make sure that you CHILL the balls. then melt the chocolate on low heat or microwave and my method of dipping (so that the balls wouldn't fall apart and get the chocolate all dirty) was to take two spoons and kind of roll it around / spoon chocolate onto the ball. 

(that's because the toothpick into an oreo ball sometimes causes the entire thing to fall apart)

I have been making these Oreo Truffles for years, and have used all different flavors of sandwich cookies...from Nutter Butter to Coffee & Cream Oreos. Each is delicious. My favorite batch is the one where I add crushed BUTTERFINGER to the Peanutbutter Oreo cookie mixture. I use about 2-3 regular sized candy bars to 1 pkg Oreos. There are so many options with this recipe...

So easy. After reading reviews, I used nutter butter cookies and put the entire bag in a processor to pulverize. I then added the room temp cream cheese and blended with the cookies in the processor. meanwhile, I microwaved the chocolate in a plastic bowl and used a small spoon and fork to drop the small peanut balls in to the chocolate. They stayed firm and I had no issues with them falling apart. I put them on a wax paper covered cookie sheet after dipping them into the chocolate. I also bought caramel peanuts and crushed them and sprinkled them on top of the finished balls before I put in the fridge. They look great, they taste great and they were super easy.

I have been making these for over 20 years and I use the whole package of oreos, double stuffed as they are more decadent tasting, and a brick of cream cheese. I do melt 2 packages of semi sweet chocolate chips and there is some left over chocolate which I just save to add to homemade hot chocolate. I put the balls in the freezer for a bit before dipping them in the chocolate that way they don't fall apart when dipping. If you want them decorative, you have somebody help you and put holiday sprinkles on them before the chocolate hardens. Usually it's my daughter helping me and she loves doing that part of it. We've made them for Christmas, Valentines day and Easter for school, Family or church functions and there are never any left over.

So easy and so fantastic! I put the truffles in the freezer for 10 minutes before coating with Ghirardelli melting wafers, used a fork to roll them and a spoon to cover any missed spots, so no problems at all with them falling apart while coating.

I have been making these for years for events, holidays and kids gifts. I dip into dark, milk and white chocolate for variation and have experimented with different flavor additions over the years. A few favorites are adding a few drops of mint extract to the cream cheese and cookie mixture and then sprinkling broken candy cane dust on top, substituting half the cream cheese for peanut butter and topping with crushed salted peanuts, and using vanilla Oreos and adding lots of lime zest and a little lime juice and topping with graham cracker crumbs and lime zest for key lime truffles.

These are ah-mazing! I tried the 'batter' and thought they weren't so great.... but the finished product was fantastic.

I added a few peppermint Dove squares which gave a great subtle peppermint flavor. I would totally do this again.

I think next time I would set aside less cookie crumbs as I had more than enough left over. From 9 i would probably do 6 and thus add more to the mix.

I used Newman's wheat free "oreos" and it turned out well, just not as many "balls" since there are less cookies in the container. I'm a big fan of this recipe.

This was one of the easiest dessert recipes I’ve ever made. I tweaked it a little bit by adding white chocolate on top of the truffles and adding a small spoonful of shortening to both chocolates as they melted on the stovetop on low heat, whisking continuously. The chocolate cured perfectly. I kept them in the fridge until ready to eat and they turned out great. I’ve been asked several times to make them again.

These were really good! Definitely placing them into the freezer for 15 minutes before coating in chocolate was helpful. You have to be careful not letting the chocolate be too thick on the rolled balls when you dip them. It was somewhat hard to work with the melted chocolate with rolling them. Fun trying different decorating toppings. Crushed peppermint candy on top of some of them gave a nice flavor. Thanks for the recipe!! :)

These are a holiday favorite around my house! I recommend using double stuff Oreos (these have never fallen apart for me), and making a batch using white chocolate bark, which is my favorite, and another with semi-sweet chocolate bark, which seems to be a hit with the kids. For anyone who does not have a food processor, I made these in my mixer for years, using the paddle attachment, and that worked well. Also, I've found that using two spoons helps when dipping the balls into the chocolate, so that you can completely cover them as you gently roll and scoop them through the chocolate. Add sprinkles for a fun and fancy garnish and people will believe you spent hours making them!

I decided to mix this up and use the peppermint Oreos. It was a wonderful twist! I will say that I struggled at first because the batter was too soft to effectively dip in the chocolate. So I rolled the truffles into balls and put them in the freezer for about 25 minutes. I used chocolate chips that I melted in the microwave and they worked just as well. The only thing you have to be careful of is, make sure you are generous when dipping the balls or they will just end up frustrating you.???

I’ve made these in the past using a different recipe and they were delicious. But these were extremely sweet and most likely inedible. I used 45 Oreos as stated in the “recipe tip” box above the recipe. So I’m guessing thats why they’re so sweet as the cookie to cream cheese ratio is off. After researching- every other recipe says, 34 cookies are needed. The “recipe tip” recommending 45 cookies- needs to be removed.
I used white chocolate. So great!

Simple and always a crowd pleaser. I now use a tablespoon measuring spoon to maintain the same size after a couple attempts of some being a bit too big. I'm going to try using a chocolate mold next time to get fun shapes and freeze the mixture before dropping in chocolate.

I love making these! I’ve made them a couple of times for my coworkers around the holidays and everyone loves them! Definitely freeze the balls for 15-20 minutes before coating them with chocolate. I freeze for 20 minutes. I use candy melts as opposed to melted semi sweet chocolate chips, but I’m sure either one is fine. I top them with red and green sanding sugar instead of the remaining cookie crumbs because I make these for Christmas. My chocolate work isn’t perfect on them at times, lol, but they taste amazing!
Love the recipe and all the variations that can be made. But to be honest the original Oreos with milk chocolate is the best! Thanks for the recipe.
How do people get 42? I got like 12...

Super easy recipe. We made them for Christmas last year and used white chocolate for our coating and then decorated with Christmas sprinkles. We brought them out for the family gathering on Christmas Eve. Big hit.

My Beba (retired confectioner) decided to make me some of these delicious OREO BALLS for my 18th Birthday. She added some lolli-pop sticks to them and added a few embellisments. I definitely give this recipe FIVE STARS! Thanks, Beba they are super delicious & pretty, too.
